dedupe_keys.name: doe oe 417 electric emergency incident and disturbance reports us major disturbance event summaries 2000 onwards

description: Form OE-417, now DOE-417, the Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report, is the form on which major electric disturbances and unusual occurrences in the United States are reported to the Department of Energy, and its annual summaries list large US grid events. The EIA archive page, titled Major Disturbances and Unusual Occurrences, offers yearly PDF summaries from 1999 to 2022 and Excel tables for 2002 to 2013, last updated in September 2022; the reports are filed through the DOE-417 web form hosted by PNNL, and the ORNL Open Energy Data Portal lists the 2023 annual summary as a public domain table. Research data sets built on it, such as the Purdue major outage file, use the event date and time, state, cause, demand loss and customers affected that the summaries report. Coverage is the United States. Files are free; US government data is in the public domain. Caveats: the DOE CESER annual summary site could not be reached on the day of cataloguing, so recent years should be taken from the reporting site or portals, and fields are self-reported by utilities. Simulation uses are event catalogues for outage risk models, attack and weather impact studies and validating restoration models. Related records: data-ecoda-event-correlated-outage-dataset-america and data-purdue-major-power-outage-risks-us are built on these reports.
